entry.value: LIMMA differential analysis%%00010===========================%%00010%%00010This component performs differential analysis using LIMMA (Linear Models for Microarray and Omics Data). It is intended primarily for normalized, log-transformed, single-channel-style quantitative data, including quantitative proteomics data.%%00010%%00010For each input row, the component fits a linear model using limma::lmFit() with least-squares fitting, applies the requested contrasts using contrasts.fit(), and performs empirical Bayes moderation using eBayes().%%00010%%00010The following experimental-design scenarios are supported:%%00010%%00010- Multiple independent experimental groups%%00010- Paired samples represented as an additive fixed-effect nuisance factor%%00010- Sample blocks or batches represented as an additive fixed-effect nuisance factor%%00010- Simultaneous adjustment for paired-sample and sample-block factors%%00010- One-sample testing of pre-calculated log ratios against zero%%00010%%00010Pairs and blocks are included in the design matrix as categorical fixed effects. They are therefore used to adjust the group comparisons for systematic differences between pairs or blocks.%%00010%%00010This implementation does not estimate within-pair or within-block correlation using duplicateCorrelation(), and it should not be interpreted as a mixed-effects model.%%00010%%00010The component validates:%%00010%%00010- The number of group, pair and block labels against the number of selected data columns%%00010- Experimental-group names used in contrasts%%00010- Design-matrix rank%%00010- Residual degrees of freedom%%00010- Duplicate and zero-valued contrasts%%00010- Contrast estimability%%00010- Linear dependence among jointly tested contrasts%%00010%%00010Clearer error messages are generated when the requested model or contrast cannot be estimated.%%00010%%00010The component can automatically generate volcano plots and p-value distribution plots for individual contrasts. Output graph filenames use filesystem-safe versions of the test and contrast names, while the original names are retained in graph subtitles and result-column references.%%00010%%00010For more information about LIMMA models, contrasts and experimental designs, see the LIMMA User's Guide:%%00010%%00010https://www.bioconductor.org/packages/release/bioc/vignettes/limma/inst/doc/usersguide.pdf%%00010%%00010%%00010Required input and configuration%%00010================================%%00010%%00010Several related inputs are required for correct analysis.%%00010%%00010%%00010Data columns%%00010------------%%00010%%00010Select the quantitative data columns to be used in the LIMMA model.%%00010%%00010The selected columns must be in the same order as the labels entered in the Experimental design, Samples pairs and Samples blocks settings.%%00010%%00010The input data are expected to be:%%00010%%00010- Numeric%%00010- Appropriately normalized%%00010- Log transformed%%00010%%00010Any logarithm base may be used, but the resulting logFC values will be expressed on the same logarithmic scale as the input data.%%00010%%00010The component does not perform normalization or log transformation automatically.%%00010%%00010%%00010Use only cases quantified in at least the specified number of replicates in at least one sample group?%%00010------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------%%00010%%00010This option filters rows before statistical analysis according to the number of observed values within the experimental groups.%%00010%%00010A common minimum-replicate threshold can be applied to all groups, or separate thresholds can be specified for individual groups.%%00010%%00010This filtering can be useful for removing rows with insufficient quantitative information before model fitting.%%00010%%00010%%00010Experimental design%%00010-------------------%%00010%%00010Enter the experimental-group name corresponding to every selected data column, in exactly the same order as the selected columns.%%00010%%00010Replicate numbers should not be included unless they are genuinely part of the experimental-group name.%%00010%%00010Example:%%00010%%00010A,A,A,B,B,B,C,C,C%%00010%%00010This represents three replicates in each of the groups A, B and C.%%00010%%00010Experimental-group names must be valid R coefficient names because they are used directly in LIMMA contrast expressions.%%00010%%00010Recommended group names contain:%%00010%%00010- Letters%%00010- Numbers%%00010- Underscores%%00010- Dots%%00010%%00010Names should not:%%00010%%00010- Contain spaces%%00010- Contain slashes%%00010- Contain mathematical operators such as + or -%%00010- Begin with a number%%00010- Contain parentheses or other contrast-expression syntax%%00010%%00010Examples of suitable group names include:%%00010%%00010Control%%00010Treatment%%00010Group_1%%00010Condition.low%%00010%%00010The number of design labels must equal the number of selected data columns.%%00010%%00010%%00010Samples pairs%%00010-------------%%00010%%00010Use this field when measurements are naturally paired, for example when two or more samples originate from the same subject, donor or biological unit.%%00010%%00010Samples belonging to the same pair must have the same identifier.%%00010%%00010Example:%%00010%%000101,2,3,1,2,3%%00010%%00010This describes three pairs, with the first and fourth columns belonging to pair 1, the second and fifth columns belonging to pair 2, and the third and sixth columns belonging to pair 3.%%00010%%00010The pair identifiers are included in the model as an additive fixed-effect nuisance factor. Group comparisons are therefore adjusted for systematic differences between pairs.%%00010%%00010Enter:%%00010%%00010none%%00010%%00010when paired-sample adjustment is not required.%%00010%%00010The number of pair identifiers must equal the number of selected data columns.%%00010%%00010Pair identifiers are intended for model adjustment and should normally not be included in the Comparisons field.%%00010%%00010%%00010Samples blocks%%00010--------------%%00010%%00010Use this field to adjust for known categorical nuisance effects such as:%%00010%%00010- Sample-preparation batches%%00010- Measurement batches%%00010- Plates%%00010- Processing days%%00010- Other known blocks spanning multiple experimental groups%%00010%%00010Samples belonging to the same block must have the same identifier.%%00010%%00010Example:%%00010%%00010batch1,batch1,batch1,batch2,batch2,batch2,batch3,batch3,batch3%%00010%%00010The block identifiers are included in the model as an additive fixed-effect nuisance factor. Experimental-group comparisons are therefore adjusted for systematic differences between blocks.%%00010%%00010Enter:%%00010%%00010none%%00010%%00010when block adjustment is not required.%%00010%%00010The number of block identifiers must equal the number of selected data columns.%%00010%%00010Block identifiers are intended for nuisance-effect adjustment and should normally not be included in the Comparisons field.%%00010%%00010Experimental variables of biological interest, such as treatment, genotype, concentration, dose or time point, should not normally be entered as blocks. Such variables should instead be represented by the experimental-group definitions and the requested contrasts.%%00010%%00010%%00010Using pairs and blocks together%%00010-------------------------------%%00010%%00010Pairs and blocks can be included simultaneously. Both are then represented as additive fixed-effect nuisance factors.%%00010%%00010The resulting model must retain sufficient residual degrees of freedom and the pair, block and group effects must be distinguishable from one another.%%00010%%00010For example, a pair factor that is perfectly confounded with an experimental group cannot be separated from the group effect.%%00010%%00010The component checks the design-matrix rank and reports non-estimable coefficients or contrasts where possible.%%00010%%00010%%00010Comparisons%%00010-----------%%00010%%00010Specify the LIMMA contrasts to be tested, separated by commas.%%00010%%00010Examples:%%00010%%00010B-A,C-A%%00010%%00010The contrast:%%00010%%00010B-A%%00010%%00010means that the average value of group A is subtracted from the average value of group B.%%00010%%00010For log-transformed input data, subtraction on the log scale corresponds to a ratio on the original scale. A positive logFC for B-A therefore indicates higher abundance in B than in A.%%00010%%00010More complex LIMMA contrasts are also supported, including:%%00010%%00010(A-B)-(C-D)%%00010%%00010This represents a difference of differences.%%00010%%00010Arithmetic expressions can contain parentheses and operators such as:%%00010%%00010+%%00010-%%00010*%%00010/%%00010%%00010Spaces surrounding operators are allowed but are not required.%%00010%%00010%%00010Factorial experimental designs%%00010------------------------------%%00010%%00010Experiments containing more than one biological factor can be represented by defining each combination of factor levels as a separate experimental group.%%00010%%00010For example, a two-factor experiment with control and treatment samples measured under two conditions could contain four experimental groups.%%00010%%00010Condition-specific treatment effects can then be tested as separate contrasts:%%00010%%00010Treatment_1-Control_1%%00010%%00010Treatment_2-Control_2%%00010%%00010The average treatment effect across the two conditions can be tested using:%%00010%%00010((Treatment_1-Control_1)+(Treatment_2-Control_2))/2%%00010%%00010An interaction, testing whether the treatment effect differs between conditions, can be specified as:%%00010%%00010(Treatment_2-Control_2)-(Treatment_1-Control_1)%%00010%%00010The condition or concentration variable should not be entered as a sample block when it represents an experimental factor of biological interest.%%00010%%00010%%00010Treat comparisons separately?%%00010-----------------------------%%00010%%00010When this option is selected, every specified contrast is reported separately.%%00010%%00010For each contrast, LIMMA calculates:%%00010%%00010- The contrast estimate or logFC%%00010- A moderated t-statistic%%00010- A raw p-value%%00010- A multiple-testing-adjusted p-value%%00010- A B-statistic, where available%%00010%%00010This is the appropriate option when the individual direction and magnitude of every comparison should be reported and interpreted.%%00010%%00010%%00010Joint ANOVA-like testing%%00010------------------------%%00010%%00010When Treat comparisons separately? is not selected, all specified contrasts are tested together using a moderated F-test.%%00010%%00010The joint null hypothesis is:%%00010%%00010All specified contrasts are equal to zero.%%00010%%00010For example, jointly testing:%%00010%%00010B-A,C-A%%00010%%00010asks whether at least one of these two contrasts differs from zero.%%00010%%00010This mode is ANOVA-like, but its meaning is determined entirely by the supplied contrasts. It is not automatically equivalent to a complete one-way ANOVA.%%00010%%00010To perform an overall test across G experimental groups, G-1 linearly independent contrasts spanning the complete group effect are generally required.%%00010%%00010For four groups, a complete overall test therefore generally requires three independent contrasts, for example:%%00010%%00010B-A,C-A,D-A%%00010%%00010Using only two contrasts for four groups tests only the hypotheses represented by those two contrasts. It does not generally test whether all four group means are equal.%%00010%%00010At least two contrasts must be supplied for joint testing.%%00010%%00010If some supplied contrasts are linearly dependent, the component reports the effective contrast rank and performs the test using the independent information contained in the contrast set.%%00010%%00010%%00010Important note about missing values%%00010===================================%%00010%%00010LIMMA handles missing values separately for each input row and fits the model using the observations available for that row.%%00010%%00010A row can nevertheless produce missing statistical results when:%%00010%%00010- Too few observations remain%%00010- No residual degrees of freedom remain%%00010- A required group coefficient cannot be estimated%%00010- The requested contrast is not estimable%%00010- The residual variance cannot be estimated%%00010- A joint test contains contrasts that cannot be evaluated for that row%%00010%%00010Rows containing no usable quantitative values cannot be statistically evaluated.%%00010%%00010Because the complete selected data matrix is used to define the model, rows observed only in a restricted subset of the experimental groups can have row-specific estimability limitations.%%00010%%00010When only a subset of groups is relevant to a particular analysis and unrelated groups contain extensive missingness, it may be preferable to run a separate LIMMA analysis using only the relevant data columns.%%00010%%00010The replicate-presence filtering option can be used to remove insufficiently quantified rows before model fitting.%%00010%%00010%%00010Log ratios test?%%00010================%%00010%%00010When this option is selected, the input matrix is interpreted as pre-calculated log-transformed ratios that should be tested for a difference from zero.%%00010%%00010This corresponds to a moderated one-sample test.%%00010%%00010In this mode:%%00010%%00010- Experimental-group contrasts are not required%%00010- Pair information is not used%%00010- Block information is not used%%00010- The input values should already represent the ratios of interest on a logarithmic scale%%00010%%00010A single experimental-design label may still be required when the component's replicate-presence filtering functionality is used.%%00010%%00010%%00010Calculate categorical evaluation-related columns?%%00010=================================================%%00010%%00010This option calculates additional columns intended for categorical interpretation of the results.%%00010%%00010These can include:%%00010%%00010- The number of observed numerical values in each compared sample group%%00010- A categorical result based on the user-defined category labels and statistical thresholds%%00010%%00010These columns are calculated only when:%%00010%%00010- Two experimental groups are compared%%00010- The analysis is not performed in log-ratio mode%%00010%%00010%%00010P-value adjustment method%%00010=========================%%00010%%00010Select the method used to correct p-values for multiple hypothesis testing.%%00010%%00010The selected method is passed to LIMMA's topTable() function, which applies R's p.adjust() functionality.%%00010%%00010The Benjamini-Hochberg method is commonly used to control the expected false discovery rate, but the most appropriate adjustment method depends on the intended analysis and interpretation.%%00010%%00010%%00010Test name%%00010=========%%00010%%00010The user-defined test name is used as a prefix for newly created result columns.%%00010%%00010The test name and contrast expressions are also used in graph labels.%%00010%%00010For graph filenames, a separate filesystem-safe representation is generated automatically. Unsupported filename characters and mathematical operators are replaced or removed without changing the original test name or contrast used for statistical result-column selection.%%00010%%00010%%00010Output statistics%%00010=================%%00010%%00010Individual-contrast output%%00010--------------------------%%00010%%00010When comparisons are treated separately, the output for each contrast can contain the following LIMMA statistics.%%00010%%00010%%00010logFC%%00010-----%%00010%%00010The estimated contrast on the logarithmic scale of the input data.%%00010%%00010For a simple B-A comparison, logFC represents the estimated mean value in B minus the estimated mean value in A, after adjustment for any pair or block fixed effects included in the model.%%00010%%00010For a complex contrast, logFC represents the complete linear combination specified by the contrast expression.%%00010%%00010When the input data are log2 transformed, this value is a log2 fold change. When another logarithm base is used, the value remains on that input logarithmic scale.%%00010%%00010%%00010AveExpr%%00010-------%%00010%%00010The average log abundance or log expression for the row across the input samples used in the fitted data matrix.%%00010%%00010%%00010t%%00010-%%00010%%00010The moderated t-statistic for the specified contrast.%%00010%%00010%%00010P.Value%%00010-------%%00010%%00010The unadjusted p-value associated with the moderated t-statistic.%%00010%%00010Because one statistical test is performed for every input row, raw p-values should normally not be used as the primary significance criterion without considering multiple hypothesis testing.%%00010%%00010%%00010adj.P.Val%%00010---------%%00010%%00010The p-value adjusted for multiple hypothesis testing using the selected adjustment method.%%00010%%00010%%00010B%%00010-%%00010%%00010The log odds that the row is differentially abundant or expressed for the specified contrast.%%00010%%00010The B-statistic may not be present for all analysis modes.%%00010%%00010%%00010Joint-test output%%00010-----------------%%00010%%00010When multiple contrasts are tested together, the output can contain:%%00010%%00010- An estimated coefficient or logFC column for each supplied contrast%%00010- AveExpr%%00010- F%%00010- P.Value%%00010- adj.P.Val%%00010%%00010%%00010F%%00010-%%00010%%00010The moderated F-statistic for the joint hypothesis that all selected contrasts are equal to zero.%%00010%%00010The F-statistic is non-directional. It indicates evidence that at least one supplied contrast differs from zero but does not by itself identify which contrast is responsible or the direction of the change.%%00010%%00010%%00010P.Value%%00010-------%%00010%%00010The unadjusted p-value associated with the moderated joint F-statistic.%%00010%%00010%%00010adj.P.Val%%00010---------%%00010%%00010The joint-test p-value adjusted across all tested input rows using the selected multiple-testing method.%%00010%%00010%%00010Automatically generated graphs%%00010==============================%%00010%%00010P-value distribution plots%%00010--------------------------%%00010%%00010P-value distribution plots can be generated for individual contrasts and for the joint moderated F-test.%%00010%%00010Original contrast expressions are used in graph subtitles. A sanitized filename-safe version is used for saving the image.%%00010%%00010%%00010Volcano plots%%00010-------------%%00010%%00010A conventional volcano plot combines:%%00010%%00010- A signed effect estimate on the x-axis%%00010- Statistical significance on the y-axis%%00010%%00010Volcano plots are therefore directly interpretable for individual contrasts with one associated logFC.%%00010%%00010A joint moderated F-test does not have one signed effect estimate. A conventional volcano plot should therefore not be interpreted as representing the complete joint test unless a specific contrast or another explicitly defined effect-size measure has been selected for its x-axis.%%00010%%00010%%00010Volcano-plot configuration%%00010==========================%%00010%%00010P-value type%%00010------------%%00010%%00010Select whether the volcano plot uses:%%00010%%00010- Raw p-values%%00010- Adjusted p-values%%00010%%00010Adjusted p-values are selected by default.%%00010%%00010%%00010Zero p-value replacement%%00010------------------------%%00010%%00010Specify the value used to replace zero p-values before calculating the negative base-10 logarithm.%%00010%%00010When zero is selected as the replacement value, rows with zero p-values cannot be converted to a finite logarithmic value and are therefore not plotted.%%00010%%00010%%00010P-value and logFC thresholds%%00010----------------------------%%00010%%00010These thresholds determine which points are categorized as statistically significant and sufficiently changed.%%00010%%00010The significance and fold-change thresholds are also used by the automatic point-labelling options.%%00010%%00010%%00010Annotation column%%00010-----------------%%00010%%00010Select the column containing the labels used to annotate points in the volcano plot.%%00010%%00010%%00010Automatic point labelling%%00010-------------------------%%00010%%00010Three principal automatic-labelling modes are available.%%00010%%00010%%00010None, manual only%%00010-----------------%%00010%%00010Only points explicitly entered in the Manual point labelling field are labelled.%%00010%%00010The entered values must match values in the selected annotation column.%%00010%%00010%%00010All significant%%00010---------------%%00010%%00010All points meeting the selected significance and change criteria are labelled.%%00010%%00010The Use thresholds to label points? setting can restrict labels to significantly changed points on one or both sides of the volcano plot.%%00010%%00010Manual point labels can be combined with this option.%%00010%%00010%%00010Top N%%00010-----%%00010%%00010The selected number of highest-ranking points is labelled.%%00010%%00010The ranking method is controlled by the Top N ranking criteria setting.%%00010%%00010The Use thresholds to label points? setting can restrict the candidates to points meeting the selected significance and direction criteria.%%00010%%00010When fewer than N points fulfil the criteria, only the available qualifying points are labelled.%%00010%%00010Manual point labels can be combined with this option.%%00010%%00010%%00010Software and licensing%%00010======================%%00010%%00010The following software and tools are used by the component.
